qs.q: A 62-year-old man with a complex enterocutaneous fistula is receiving nutritional support. For a high-output proximal small bowel fistula that requires complete bowel rest, what is the preferred route of nutrition?
qs.e: Total parenteral nutrition is indicated for high-output proximal small bowel fistulas to allow complete bowel rest. Oral and enteral routes are preferred when the fistula is more distal or colonic.
qs.s: Intestinal and Enterocutaneous Fistulas: Classification and Management: MCQs

qs.q: A premature infant with Bell stage IIA necrotising enterocolitis is placed on nil by mouth. For how long is enteral feeding typically withheld as part of the primary bowel rest management?
qs.e: Management of stages I and II includes stopping all enteral feeds for 7 to 14 days to achieve bowel rest. Gastric decompression with an orogastric or nasogastric tube is also maintained.
qs.s: Necrotising Enterocolitis in the Newborn: MCQs

qs.q: An infant receiving total parenteral nutrition and broad-spectrum antibiotics for stage II necrotising enterocolitis develops direct hyperbilirubinaemia and conjugated jaundice. Which aspect of the ongoing management plan is the direct cause of bowel rest?
o: Maintain nil per os for seven to fourteen days
Place an orogastric tube with low intermittent suction
Perform serial abdominal examinations every four hours
qs.e: Bowel rest is achieved by stopping all enteral feeds (nil by mouth) for 7 to 14 days. Gastric decompression uses an orogastric or nasogastric tube, but the cessation of feeds is the defining feature of bowel rest.
qs.s: Necrotising Enterocolitis in the Newborn: MCQs
